candidate_issuer_epoch.issuer_epoch_identity: HQ-adopted issuer exact identity + one immutable provisioned deployment epoch ref, allocated and approved only after HQ adoption
candidate_issuer_epoch.root_bootstrap: Only the future HQ-approved exact HQ_AT07_ISSUER_ROOT_APPROVAL_RECEIPT@2 plus separately installed verifier read root and explicit HQ activation authorize epoch. Never caller/registrar root, latest branch, unsigned-looking unapproved map or hash alone.
candidate_issuer_epoch.registrar_write_capability: Exact C1 owner writer identity in HQ approved and activated bootstrap record, privileged and not public, cannot approve itself.
candidate_issuer_epoch.verifier_read_capability: Trusted deployment pin independently rooted in HQ-approved exact commit + root-placement digest and independent verifier acknowledgment, not the untrusted registry being checked.
candidate_issuer_epoch.attestation_choice: OWNER_JOURNAL_MEMBERSHIP_WITH_TRUSTED_BOOTSTRAP, not a claim of a cryptographic signature. Signed credentials permitted only under separately approved key custody; no key generated by this proposal.
candidate_issuer_epoch.rotation: HQ-approved explicit prior→successor record and HQ activation; no overlap/fork without explicit HQ law; exact historical audit only for revoked epochs

canonical_ref_rules.future_references: All exact refs are kind+object_id+content_hash under admitted PRE553 canonical JSON SHA256; no authority by hash alone; runtime registry membership and provenance required
canonical_ref_rules.build_identity: Candidate kind C1_AT07_FIXTURE_BUILD_INSTANCE@1; proposed object_id from unique (issuer epoch, persistent atomic sequence, source build provenance); preimage retains owner event + fixture content hashes; one content-identical but separately built source consumes a DIFFERENT persistent event sequence and DIFFERENT build ref
canonical_ref_rules.build_sequence: Owner-allocated persisted monotone sequence within unique issuer epoch, atomic reservation/commit, no reset/reuse after restart/revocation, no reliance on process-local nonce alone; collision is refusal not overwriting
canonical_ref_rules.credential_identity: Candidate kind C1_AT07_FIXTURE_USE_CONTEXT@1; digest over issued use-event material including build_ref, full invocation refs, use-site, original registered issuer epoch/warrant, exact source/release and witness, status_at_issuance; never hash a payload that includes its own digest
canonical_ref_rules.registry_membership: Verifier must match exact original journal record by full ref and content, issuer epoch and deployment root, and must read current negative lifecycle state independently; no latest/default/fallback
canonical_ref_rules.collision: Duplicate event_id or (issuer epoch, sequence) with different preimage => integrity conflict. Duplicate context_id with different scope => refuse. Distinct sequence for identical fixture content => distinct identity; cannot equate or exchange
canonical_ref_rules.metadata_is_not_semantic_time: registration event sequence, issued_at and optional expiry are credential lifecycle data; never substitute snapshot static AT07_FIXTURE_ONLY or conditioner actual null effective context

transitions.requires: C1 owned ingress, no handoff ref
exact ACTIVE C1 parent, unique original build and witness, authenticated N10E recipient
REQUIRED_NON_NULL_ISSUER_JOURNAL_HANDOFF_REF and same exact ancestor build/invocation; registered receiver use
full active ancestry revalidated, no cached currentness
authorized immutable issuer/HQ negative receipt as applicable; preserve exact historical audit
no reactivation/reuse; separate issuer-epoch approval and fresh exact issued identity required

lifecycle.expiry: No default expiry duration invented. A registered explicit expiry boundary, if adopted, must be identity-bearing and verified using trusted operational validity metadata; otherwise null means no scheduled expiry, NOT forever-current against revocation
lifecycle.revoke: Explicit authorized event invalidates future current-use checks for affected build/context/issuer epoch; cascading dependent contexts fail closed
lifecycle.issuer_revocation: Revoking issuer epoch blocks new registrations and current positive uses unless a separately adopted historical-grace rule exists; none proposed. Archived root remains usable for evidence-only historical audit
lifecycle.reissuance: Fresh event, fresh identity and explicitly authorized lineage; historical credential refs remain immutable and NOT current. Never silent reuse of same object_id or automatic migration
lifecycle.replay: Current-positive N10E replay resolves pinned same original issuer/build/site credential and current status; revoked/expired returns owned authority exception. Separate audit-only historical reproduction MAY verify archived proof as historical explanation but never produce CURRENT results or new use grants; no default latest issuer
lifecycle.no_retroactive_output_relabel: Past immutable receipts preserved exactly; changing eligibility does not rewrite historical semantic result state, only current-use permission

verifier_algorithm: Check trusted deployment-embedded HQ immutable approval/activation refs against independently authenticated HQ governance installation record and digest, not a caller-supplied URL/ref alone.

Resolve exact approved warrant, designated C1 owner assembly, issuer epoch, root/journal genesis, expected writer/read principals and placement manifest; require matching immutable HQ authority event(s) and explicit ACTIVE approval.
Read root material from independently provisioned verifier read placement; bytes and journal genesis hash must exactly match HQ approved and activated content.
Reject absent, stale, revoked, unactivated, forked or competing roots; no 'choose one that validates', latest/default or self-signed content acceptance.
Validate owner-journal events by membership in this exact activated journal plus unique event sequence and issuer capability provenance, never by SHA256 alone.
Resolve issuer/caller currentness against exact governed activation and revocation checkpoint independently of a cached request body.
Trusted verifier root independently provisioned and ACTIVE under exact HQ approval; never supplied by request
Resolve all five required journal ancestors: build → invocation → C1 site → owner-issued handoff → N10E site, plus root activation

Compare full exact issuer/warrant/epoch, original build/ref receipt, direction-specific producer query/predicate hash, consumer query, conditioner fingerprint and entire 16-key witness identity across every parent and live request
Check R8 release, universe, manifest, synthetic owner provenance and actual canonical-null conditioner/witness against their own exact refs
Check C1 site token and N10E site token separately; derive N10E receiver ingress from approved deployment callsite, not supplied label
Require handoff ref non-null, exact kind, current owner-journal membership, owner-issued producer transition and active parent; refuse a copied syntactic ExactRef
Check independent currentness of HQ issuer epoch, C1 site event, handoff event and N10E event; revoked/expired/stale parent refuses positive current use
Before provider request acceptance and before composition/replay, verify exact same build_instance_ref and all parent refs, not merely equal R8 rows/output hashes

Record issuer activation, original build, C1 site, handoff, N10E use and witness as genuinely consumed context determinants on BOTH provider EXACT and REFUSED receipts, result/replay identities and C1-03R dependency registration (Z06 retains semantic authority revision jurisdiction)

attacker_boundary.attacker: Ordinary untrusted caller, request arguments, raw mappings, fixture rows, copied or syntactically valid ExactRef/receipt, and caller-controlled test helper outputs
attacker_boundary.trusted: HQ-adopted exact warrant bootstrap, owner-controlled registrar journal, verifier independently provisioned from governance-approved trusted deployment root; no authority from user-provided payload
attacker_boundary.not_defended: Arbitrary hostile Python code execution with write access to registrar/verifier process memory, monkeypatching privileged modules, malicious deployment maintainer or compromised HQ governance. Python-private state alone is not a cryptographic security boundary against hostile code.
attacker_boundary.fork_if_required: If code-compromise/F7-style adversary is in scope, separate service/signed attestation and independently verified key custody need distinct HQ warrant; this bounded proposal does not claim it
attacker_boundary.guarantee: Owner/data authority provenance against caller self-attestation, not general adversarial process-security

bootstrap_approval_contract.scope: ONE source-free AT07 fixture-use issuer, its owner journal and two callsite grants only; not a generic HQ or semantic authority framework

HQ_DECISION_OWNER.identity: PYAT HQ explicit governance-adoption and deployment-root adjudicator
HQ_DECISION_OWNER.authority_scope: MAY prospectively adopt this narrow warrant and authorize exactly one initially active issuer epoch/bootstrap record or future explicit rotation/revocation by immutable HQ approval; NOT a power delegated by R8 hashes
HQ_DECISION_OWNER.proof: Exact HQ-approved immutable governance record/commit bound to adopted warrant, epoch, candidate owner and deployment-root manifest. No worker proposal is an HQ decision.

C1_OWNER_ASSEMBLY.identity: SINGLE later HQ-designated C1-01 source-free fixture-owner assembly, exact owner_assembly_ref is issued in HQ bootstrap approval
C1_OWNER_ASSEMBLY.authority_scope: Prepare sealed root proposal/empty owner journal genesis, provision authorized registrar writer and route-bound C1 ingress only AFTER HQ permission; cannot approve its own root
C1_OWNER_ASSEMBLY.proof: Owner-controlled deployment identity and journal genesis must match HQ-approved digest and subsequent active epoch; pytest and N10E helpers are not this assembly.

ROOT_PLACEMENT_OPERATOR.identity: Approved deployment/placement function OF THE NAMED C1 owner assembly, not an independently self-appointing authority
ROOT_PLACEMENT_OPERATOR.authority_scope: Copy exactly HQ-approved immutable root bytes and pinned metadata into verifier trusted deployment artifact. No ability to alter approved root or select issuer by latest.
ROOT_PLACEMENT_OPERATOR.proof: Exact placement receipt with approved manifest ref, installed digest, owner deployment ref and independent verifier acknowledgement. Requires HQ activation; not a new positive semantic role.

VERIFIER.identity: One separately provisioned AT07 verifier read role pinned to HQ-approved root placement
VERIFIER.authority_scope: Read trusted HQ placement and immutable owner journal, check current epoch and complete registered event chain; cannot mint/bootstrap/rotate/authorize itself
VERIFIER.proof: Verifier obtains immutable root pin from adopted HQ-governed deployment/installation manifest supplied through its trusted installation channel independent of request, registrar response or caller mapping.

REGISTRAR.identity: One C1-owned writer role bound to exact approved epoch and registrar_write_capability_id
REGISTRAR.authority_scope: After HQ activation, atomically register BUILD, INVOCATION, C1 SITE, HANDOFF and N10E SITE events only at authenticated owner callsite; never self-approve root or epoch
REGISTRAR.proof: Writer capability is sealed to approved deployment identity and epoch; no public request path grants writer privilege.

proposed_bootstrap_sequence.effect: Creates accepted immutable warrant exact ref. Absent it every subsequent root action is forbidden.

proposed_bootstrap_sequence.prerequisite: HQ-approved C1 owner designation and adopted warrant, owner preparation under trusted deployment identity
proposed_bootstrap_sequence.effect: Produce proposed unique epoch identity, genesis owner journal hash and exact immutable placement manifest including writer/read principal IDs; NO issuer activation, NO journal writes.

proposed_bootstrap_sequence.prerequisite: Explicit HQ review of exact immutable proposal; independently confirm owner boundary, source-free ceiling, journal genesis hash and unique non-reused epoch ID
proposed_bootstrap_sequence.effect: HQ commits approval_event_ref and exact complete approved root placement receipt/preimage. Only this authorizes INSTALL of those fixed bytes, not issuance.

proposed_bootstrap_sequence.effect: Registrar writer capability and independent verifier read root installed as separately authorized roles. Each creates immutable installation acknowledgment linked to HQ approval, with proof of exact approved digest; no alternative root permitted.

proposed_bootstrap_sequence.effect: Issues immutable activation_event_ref and exact active epoch state at a governed checkpoint. Only then first build journal registration may occur.

owner_root_proposal.unique_epoch_allocation_claim: Owner proposed unique unconsumed epoch_id; HQ independently checks uniqueness before approving; cannot reset even after revocation

trusted_placement.approval_to_pin: The verifier's *deployment image/config* is independently pinned to exact HQ root approval/activation records by the governed HQ-approved artifact placement. It never learns its root from a request credential, provider, test helper, registrar's response, mutable latest-branch head or self-presented registry.
verification_sequence: Check trusted deployment-embedded HQ immutable approval/activation refs against independently authenticated HQ governance installation record and digest, not a caller-supplied URL/ref alone.

Resolve exact approved warrant, designated C1 owner assembly, issuer epoch, root/journal genesis, expected writer/read principals and placement manifest; require matching immutable HQ authority event(s) and explicit ACTIVE approval.
Read root material from independently provisioned verifier read placement; bytes and journal genesis hash must exactly match HQ approved and activated content.
Reject absent, stale, revoked, unactivated, forked or competing roots; no 'choose one that validates', latest/default or self-signed content acceptance.
Validate owner-journal events by membership in this exact activated journal plus unique event sequence and issuer capability provenance, never by SHA256 alone.
Resolve issuer/caller currentness against exact governed activation and revocation checkpoint independently of a cached request body.
trusted_placement.independence_boundary: HQ-governed placement is part of trusted deployment provenance within the ordinary-untrusted-caller threat model. It is NOT a claim that arbitrary hostile privileged Python code cannot replace local modules/bytes; that stronger capability requires a separate authority/court. Root installer is a constrained C1 owner operational function, not a free actor empowered by caller.

rotation_revocation.rotate_authorizer: HQ only via HQ_APPROVE_AT07_ISSUER_ROOT_ROTATION followed by explicit HQ_ACTIVATE_AT07_ISSUER_EPOCH; C1 owner can propose but not approve/activate
rotation_revocation.rotate_preconditions: Must point to exactly active prior epoch and exact HQ-approved successor, reserve distinct successor epoch and new root, avoid concurrent unfenced writers; no key/latest rewrite. HQ activation only after independent installed verifier acknowledgment.
rotation_revocation.rotate_activation: Explicit HQ governance commit atomically specifies exact replacement active epoch and old epoch current-use termination checkpoint. Verifier MUST independently reload approved active epoch/currentness and require exact authorized credential epoch. No silent migration of old credentials.
rotation_revocation.revoke_authorizer: HQ explicit issuer-epoch revocation; for context/build site-specific revocation only separately authorized C1 registrar within still-active epoch under proposed role, append immutable reason/event
rotation_revocation.negative_propagation: Fail closed if currentness cannot be checked; epoch revocation cascades to current use of build, C1 site, handoff and N10E site. Historical provenance can be verified against exact archived approved root for AUDIT_ONLY with no new/current output.
refusal_cases: root fork with two self-consistent manifests
writer principal change without HQ approval
same epoch and duplicate sequence after restart
root tamper with matching caller hash but mismatched HQ pin

collision_and_restart.scope: For each ACTIVE unique epoch, owner journal enforces a single durable atomically allocated monotone event sequence across all kinds: BUILD, INVOCATION, C1 SITE, HANDOFF, N10E SITE and negative events. Restart may not reset allocation or change genesis; reused (epoch,seq) different preimage or duplicated event id => integrity refusal, quarantine/no overwrite.
collision_and_restart.equal_fixture_rows: Equal R8 content across two owner-approved builds still gets separately allocated BUILD event/ref; build instance not recoverable from content hash alone.
collision_and_restart.fork_rule: Two independently self-consistent roots with same warrant/epoch but divergent genesis or event history are an AUTHORITY_CONFLICT and CURRENT use refuses until HQ exact adjudication, never picks last-written or first-valid.

ignored_HQ240_site_template: Original optional cross_site_handoff_ref_or_null general schema SUPERSEDED. C1 accepts null; N10E requires non-null journal-issued event with C1 parent. No generic INVOCATION_SEALED -> SITE_USE_ACTIVE transition survives.
